questions.text: Which of the following sets of monomers is used in the synthesis of Nylon-6,6?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The nomenclature 'Nylon-6,6' indicates a polyamide formed from two different monomers each containing 6 carbon atoms: a diamine (hexamethylenediamine, 6C) and a diacid (adipic acid, 6C). Nylon-6 uses caprolactam; Bakelite uses phenol/formaldehyde; Terylene (Dacron) uses ethylene glycol/terephthalic acid. Full Solution: Nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer (polyamide) synthesized by the step-growth polymerization of hexamethylenediamine (H₂N–(CH₂)₆–NH₂) and adipic acid (HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH) with the elimination of water. The numbers 6,6 denote the number of carbon atoms in the diamine and the diacid respectively.

questions.text: If A is a non-singular square matrix of order 3 such that |A| = 5, then the value of |adj(adj A)| is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a non-singular matrix A of order n, |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n-1)^2). Here n=3, |A|=5, so value = 5^4 = 625. Full: We know adj(adj A) = |A|^(n-2) * A. Taking determinant, |adj(adj A)| = | |A|^(n-2) A | = |A|^((n-2)n) * |A| = |A|^(n^2 - 2n + 1) = |A|^((n-1)^2). Substituting n=3, |A|=5 gives 5^4 = 625.

questions.text: Which of the following transition metal ions is colorless in aqueous solution due to the absence of d-d transitions?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ions with d⁰ or d¹⁰ configuration have no d-d transitions and are colorless. Ti⁴⁺ is d⁰ (3d⁰), while V³⁺ (d²), Fe³⁺ (d⁵), Cu²⁺ (d⁹) have partially filled d-orbitals and are colored. Full solution: Electronic configuration of Ti⁴⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁰, so no d-d transition possible; hence it is colorless.

questions.text: For the gaseous reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the value of Kp is 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ atm⁻² at 500 K. The value of Kc (in mol² L⁻²) at the same temperature is closest to: (R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Δn_g = moles of gaseous products – moles of gaseous reactants = 2 – 4 = –2. Since Δn is negative, Kc = Kp(RT)². Calculate RT = 0.0821 × 500 ≈ 41. (RT)² ≈ 1681. Kc ≈ 4×10⁻⁴ × 1681 ≈ 0.67. Full Solution: The relationship is Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. Here Δn = 2 – (1+3) = –2. Rearranging, Kc = Kp(RT)² = (4.0×10⁻⁴) × (0.0821 × 500)² = 4.0×10⁻⁴ × (41.05)² ≈ 4.0×10⁻⁴ × 1685 ≈ 0.674 mol² L⁻².

questions.text: The half-life of a first order reaction is 20 minutes. The time required for 99% completion of the reaction is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a first order reaction, t_99% ≈ 6.64 × t_1/2 (since ln(100)/ln(2) ≈ 4.605/0.693 = 6.64). 20 min × 6.64 ≈ 133 min. Full solution: k = ln2 / t_1/2 = 0.693/20 min⁻¹. For 99% completion, fraction remaining = 0.01, so t = (1/k) ln(1/0.01) = (20/0.693) × 4.605 ≈ 132.8 min ≈ 133 min.

questions.text: A particle is moving with velocity v = 2t² + 3t. Find its acceleration at t = 2s.
If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, find A n B.
questions.solution: A n B = elements common to both sets = {2, 3}.

questions.text: For a diatomic ideal gas (γ = 7/5), what is the ratio of adiabatic bulk modulus to isothermal bulk modulus?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Isothermal bulk modulus B_iso = P. Adiabatic bulk modulus B_ad = γP. Ratio = γ = Cp/Cv = 7/5 = 1.4. Full: Bulk modulus B = -V(dP/dV). For isothermal process PV=constant => dP/P = -dV/V => B_iso = P. For adiabatic process PV^γ=constant => dP/P = -γ dV/V => B_ad = γP. Ratio B_ad/B_iso = γ = 1.4.

questions.text: The Boolean expression for the output Y of a logic circuit is Y = A·B + A'·B' (where ' denotes NOT). Which logic gate does this circuit represent?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The expression Y = AB + A'B' is the standard SOP form of an XNOR (Equivalence) gate. Output is HIGH (1) only when inputs are equal (A=B). Full: Truth table: A=0,B=0 => Y=1; A=0,B=1 => Y=0; A=1,B=0 => Y=0; A=1,B=1 => Y=1. This matches the XNOR gate truth table (output 1 for even number of 1s / equality).

questions.text: For a binomial distribution B(n, p), the mean is 4 and the variance is 3. The probability of at least one success is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For Binomial, q = Variance/Mean = 3/4, so p = 1/4. Then n = Mean/p = 4/(1/4) = 16. P(at least 1 success) = 1 - P(0 success) = 1 - qⁿ = 1 - (3/4)¹⁶. Full: Given np = 4 and npq = 3. Dividing, q = 3/4 ⇒ p = 1/4. Substituting in np=4 gives n(1/4)=4 ⇒ n=16. P(X ≥ 1) = 1 - P(X=0) = 1 - ⁿC₀ p⁰ qⁿ = 1 - (3/4)¹⁶.

questions.text: The value of ∫₀¹ x² dx is:

A solid sphere, a solid cylinder, and a thin ring, each of mass M and radius R, are released from rest at the top of a rough inclined plane of inclination θ. They roll without slipping. Which object reaches the bottom first?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Acceleration down an incline for rolling is a = g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²), where k is radius of gyration. The object with smallest k²/R² (sphere: 0.4) has maximum acceleration. Full: For rolling without slipping, mg sinθ - f = ma and fR = Iα = I(a/R). Solving gives a = g sinθ / (1 + I/mR²). Moments of inertia: Sphere = 2/5 mR², Cylinder = 1/2 mR², Ring = mR². Denominators are 1.4, 1.5, 2.0 respectively. Sphere has highest acceleration and reaches first.

questions.text: If the probability of an event A is 0.4 and of B is 0.5, and A and Bare independent, then P(A n B) is:
questions.solution: For independent events: P(A n B) = P(A)·P(B) = 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2.

questions.text: A convex lens has focal length 20 cm. At what distance from the lens should an object be placed to get a real image twice the size of object?
questions.solution: Magnification m = -2 (real image). m = v/u = -2 ⇒ v = -2u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. 1/20 = 1/(-2u) - 1/u = -3/(2u). u = -30 cm. So object distance = 30 cm.

questions.text: The EMF of the concentration cell Cu(s) | Cu²⁺(0.1 M) || Cu²⁺(0.01 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a concentration cell with n=2, E = (0.059/2) log₁₀(C₁/C₂). Here C₁/C₂ = 10, log10 = 1, so E = 0.0295 V. Full solution: Using Nernst equation, E = (RT/nF) ln(C₁/C₂) = (0.0591/2) log₁₀(0.1/0.01) = 0.02955 × 1 = 0.0295 V.
